docs.title: Smart Switch with Hypershield Integration Lab
docs.text:
Nexus | Cisco Live lab LTRDCN-1476

Select your assigned POD from the dropdown on this landing page. Each POD guide contains the same lab tasks and screenshots, with values specific to that lab user.

Follow the tasks in order. Use Overview for the lab topology and Troubleshooting for recovery notes.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Use Nexus Dashboard to configure tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on Cisco Smart Switches, enable Secure VRF redirection, and configure a matching allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Current review guide
docs.text: The site currently publishes the complete POD-01 guide for labusr01 for review. Once its tasks and editable values are approved, the guide can be replicated for the remaining attendees.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: The lab establishes routed connectivity first. It then enables Secure VRF and confirms switch-side Hypershield readiness. Because no matching policy is present yet, connectivity analysis may report that redirected packets did not return to the NPU. Create the scoped network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, deploy them, and rerun the analysis. Complete endpoint checks and record the observed results for your pod.

docs.title: Topology
docs.text: This topology is reproduced from the v7 lab guide. POD-01 network and endpoint values are listed in its guide.

docs.title: Task sequence
docs.text:
Task Outcome 1. Get started Open the assigned workstation, dashboard, endpoints, and switch sessions 2. Create VRF and networks Create the pod's VRF and two Layer 3 networks using its table 3. Attach and deploy Attach each network to its switch and confirm deployed state 4. Verify baseline connectivity Confirm the permitted pre-policy route and endpoint traffic 5. Enable Secure VRF Enable Dynamic DPU affinity and check switch readiness 6. Timescape objects and policy Deploy scoped objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy 7. Verify Review final analysis and record endpoint test results

During this review stage, only POD-01 is published. The other attendee pages are preserved outside the published site until POD-01 is ready to replicate.

docs.title: Address in use when starting iperf3
docs.text: The walkthrough attempted iperf3 -s -p 8080 on endpoint 2 and received Address in use. A listener was already active, and the client subsequently connected successfully. Use the existing listener. If your pod has no listener, ask the lab instructor to confirm endpoint setup before starting one.

docs.title: Packets redirected to DPU do not return to NPU
docs.text: This warning appeared after Secure VRF was enabled and before the matching Timescape policy was deployed. Confirm both switch agents are healthy, create/deploy the two VRF-scoped objects, and deploy the TCP/8080 allow rule. Rerun Connectivity Analysis afterward.

docs.title: VRF, network, or object values do not match
docs.text: Use the generated pod page as the source of attendee values. Confirm network IDs, VLAN IDs, gateway/CIDR, tenant, and VRF scope. Do not reuse values from older versions of this guide (for example vrf1112, net11, or VLAN 2000).

docs.title: Deployment does not finish
docs.text: Wait for the deployment status to settle and check configuration synchronization. Verify that both attachments point to the intended switch and Ethernet1/13, then retry only after resolving any reported validation errors.

docs.title: Evidence limitation
docs.text: The recordings show the final connectivity analysis overview and routing result, and show a single TCP/8080 allow rule on the switch. They do not show a post-policy endpoint ping/iperf3 test or an explicit post-policy security verdict. Record those test results in the live pod rather than treating them as established by the recording.

Smart Switch with Hypershield Integration Lab

Session ID: LTRDCN-1476

Speaker: Abhishek Jha

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.text: Figure 1. Portrait lab topology showing switches, host networks, ESXi, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, and controller relationships.

docs.title: Task sequence
docs.text:
1. Task 1 — Get started

  2. Task 2 — Create the VRF and networks

  3. Task 3 — Attach and deploy the networks

  4. Task 4 — Verify baseline connectivity

  5. Task 5 — Enable Secure VRF

  6. Task 6 — Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI

  7. Task 7 — Verify policy behavior

  8. Task 8 — Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Great Job! You have accomplished all the Lab Tasks. Please close any open browser tabs to keep the workspace clean.

In this lab, you explored Smart Switches and Hypershield integration and tested policy enforcement with On-prem as well as Cloud solution (SCC). You are now ready to dive deeper into these technologies and their ecosystem.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Open the assigned pod systems and confirm that the required management sessions are available.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Your event lab credentials and assigned pod number.

  • Cisco Secure Client VPN access if required by the event environment.

  • Remote Desktop Connection.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Connect to the event VPN with the IP address as per your Lab access instructions.

  2. Open Remote Desktop Connection and connect to the workstation address on the pod-specific values at the start of this guide.

  3. Sign in with the credentials provided for the lab.

  4. Open the saved browser bookmarks for Nexus Dashboard and Timescape. Dashboard is the fabric configuration interface; Timescape is used later for security objects and policies.

  5. Open MTPuTTY and locate the saved sessions for both Smart Switches and both endpoints.

  6. Review the pod-specific values in this guide. Use endpoint management addresses to connect to endpoint consoles and data addresses only for traffic tests.

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text:
Checkpoint: Confirm that you can reach the workstation, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, both Smart Switches, and both endpoints. Do not change device settings yet.

The recording begins with the applications already available and does not show VPN sign-in or account onboarding. Use the event lab instructions for credentials and initial access.

docs.title: Task 2: Create the VRF and networks
Task 2: Create the VRF and networks
Create the tenant VRF and two Layer 3 networks using the assigned pod values.
docs.text: For routed communication between VXLAN EVPN networks, create a tenant VRF associated with a Layer 3 VNI. Create each Layer 3 network with its VLAN and anycast gateway, then associate it with that VRF.

Objective

docs.title: Attach the networks
docs.text:
1. Attach vlan11 to Smart-SW-1 Ethernet1/13.

    • a. In SmartSwitch-Pod1, open Segmentation and security > Networks.

    • b. Click vlan11, then click Network Attachments.

    • c. Select the check box which has an entry of Smart-SW-1 switch, then click white Actions > Edit

    • d. In the Edit Network Attachment screen, click the slider to Attach, then under Attached interface for this device click (white) Action and click on Add network interface attachment

      Figure. Network attachment editor for vlan11.

    • e. Under Add Network Interface Attachment, filter with Smart-SW-1 and Ethernet 1/13

      Figure. Select Smart-SW-1 Ethernet1/13 for vlan11.

      Figure. Selected interface for the vlan11 attachment.

    • f. Click Add, then Save the attachment.

      Figure. vlan11 interface attachment in the edit view.

    • g. Return to the Networks view

      Figure. vlan11 attached to Smart-SW-1.

  2. Attach vlan12 to Smart-SW-2 Ethernet1/13.

    • a. Click vlan12, then open Network Attachments tab.

    • b. Select the check box which has an entry of Smart-SW-2 switch then click white Actions > Edit.

    • c. In the Edit Network Attachment screen, click the slider to Attach then under Attached interface for this device click (white) Action and click on Add network interface attachment.

    • d. Under Add Network Interface Attachment, filter with Smart-SW-2 and Ethernet 1/13

  2. Select labusr01-vrf, then choose Actions (white) > Multi-attach and select both Smart Switches and click Next.

docs.title: Verify switch readiness
docs.text:
Confirm that the output reports Agent Health Status: ok, a successful controller connection, firewall in-service, and VRF operational state forwarding ready. The recording showed Dynamic affinity and DPU 2 for labusr01-t:labusr01-vrf.

Figure. Hypershield agent and service acceleration report ready.

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.

docs.title: ICMP check: from EP-vlan11, run the ping command below and record the actual response. Ping will drop
docs.text:
vm:~$ ping 12.0.0.20
PING 12.0.0.20 (12.0.0.20): 56 data bytes

docs.text:
On EP-vlan12, start the server:

vm:~$ iperf3 -s -p 8080

On EP-vlan11, start the client:

vm:~$ iperf3 -c 12.0.0.20 -p 8080 -t 10 -b 1G

docs.title: Task 6: Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI
Task 6: Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI
Objective
docs.text: Because Secure VRF redirects traffic to a DPU, application traffic needs an explicit security policy. Create network objects for the two endpoint subnets in the lab VRF, then deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy from vlan11 to vlan12 and block rest of the traffic.

docs.title: Check the switch before policy creation
docs.text:
Before creating the policy, check the current switch state.

Open the saved Smart Switch session in MTPuTTY and run the command below to check for loaded policies:

Smart-SW-1# run bash sudo docker exec -it HypershieldAgent ./agwctl policies show
Client got: ok
Data:
No policies loaded
Smart-SW-1#

The switch reports no policies by default. Create and deploy the policy from the on-premises Hypershield (Timescape UI) controller.

Note: Since this is a shared lab, you might come across some policies already created by other lab users.

Figure. Create Object selection in Timescape.

  1. Create the two network objects using the values in the table, then Deploythem.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: The deployed policy permits TCP port 8080 between the configured networks. Other protocols, including ICMP, are not permitted by this rule and are expected to be denied.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text: • Perform the Ping test between the Endpoints EP-vlan11 (11.0.0.10) and EP-vlan12 (12.0.0.20). and it will fail as ICMP is not allowed in permit policy

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.text: Figure 1. Portrait lab topology showing switches, host networks, ESXi, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, and controller relationships.

docs.title: Task sequence
docs.text:
1. Task 1 — Get started

  2. Task 2 — Create the VRF and networks

  3. Task 3 — Attach and deploy the networks

  4. Task 4 — Verify baseline connectivity

  5. Task 5 — Enable Secure VRF

  6. Task 6 — Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI

  7. Task 7 — Verify policy behavior

  8. Task 8 — Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Great Job! You have accomplished all the Lab Tasks. Please close any open browser tabs to keep the workspace clean.

In this lab, you explored Smart Switches and Hypershield integration and tested policy enforcement with On-prem as well as Cloud solution (SCC). You are now ready to dive deeper into these technologies and their ecosystem.

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.

PING 30.0.0.20 (30.0.0.20): 56 data bytes

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: The deployed policy permits TCP port 8080 between the configured networks. Other protocols, including ICMP, are not permitted by this rule and are expected to be denied.

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.title: Topology
docs.text: Figure 1. Portrait lab topology showing switches, host networks, ESXi, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, and controller relationships.

docs.title: Task sequence
docs.text:
1. Task 1 — Get started

  2. Task 2 — Create the VRF and networks

  3. Task 3 — Attach and deploy the networks

  4. Task 4 — Verify baseline connectivity

  5. Task 5 — Enable Secure VRF

  6. Task 6 — Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI

  7. Task 7 — Verify policy behavior

  8. Task 8 — Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Great Job! You have accomplished all the Lab Tasks. Please close any open browser tabs to keep the workspace clean.

In this lab, you explored Smart Switches and Hypershield integration and tested policy enforcement with On-prem as well as Cloud solution (SCC). You are now ready to dive deeper into these technologies and their ecosystem.

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.

Task 8: Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control
Objective

docs.text:

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.title: Topology
docs.text: Figure 1. Portrait lab topology showing switches, host networks, ESXi, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, and controller relationships.

docs.title: Task sequence
docs.text:
1. Task 1 — Get started

  2. Task 2 — Create the VRF and networks

  3. Task 3 — Attach and deploy the networks

  4. Task 4 — Verify baseline connectivity

  5. Task 5 — Enable Secure VRF

  6. Task 6 — Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI

  7. Task 7 — Verify policy behavior

  8. Task 8 — Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Great Job! You have accomplished all the Lab Tasks. Please close any open browser tabs to keep the workspace clean.

In this lab, you explored Smart Switches and Hypershield integration and tested policy enforcement with On-prem as well as Cloud solution (SCC). You are now ready to dive deeper into these technologies and their ecosystem.

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.

docs.title: Task 6: Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI
Task 6: Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI
Objective
docs.text: Because Secure VRF redirects traffic to a DPU, application traffic needs an explicit security policy. Create network objects for the two endpoint subnets in the lab VRF, then deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy from vlan33 to vlan34 and block rest of the traffic.

docs.title: Check the switch before policy creation
docs.text:
Before creating the policy, check the current switch state.

Open the saved Smart Switch session in MTPuTTY and run the command below to check for loaded policies:

Smart-SW-1# run bash sudo docker exec -it HypershieldAgent ./agwctl policies show
Client got: ok
Data:
No policies loaded
Smart-SW-1#

The switch reports no policies by default. Create and deploy the policy from the on-premises Hypershield (Timescape UI) controller.

Note: Since this is a shared lab, you might come across some policies already created by other lab users.

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.title: Topology
docs.text: Figure 1. Portrait lab topology showing switches, host networks, ESXi, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, and controller relationships.

docs.title: Task sequence
docs.text:
1. Task 1 — Get started

  2. Task 2 — Create the VRF and networks

  3. Task 3 — Attach and deploy the networks

  4. Task 4 — Verify baseline connectivity

  5. Task 5 — Enable Secure VRF

  6. Task 6 — Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI

  7. Task 7 — Verify policy behavior

  8. Task 8 — Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Great Job! You have accomplished all the Lab Tasks. Please close any open browser tabs to keep the workspace clean.

In this lab, you explored Smart Switches and Hypershield integration and tested policy enforcement with On-prem as well as Cloud solution (SCC). You are now ready to dive deeper into these technologies and their ecosystem.

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.

PING 38.0.0.20 (38.0.0.20): 56 data bytes

On EP-vlan37, start the client:

vm:~$ iperf3 -c 38.0.0.20 -p 8080 -t 10 -b 1G

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.text: Figure 1. Portrait lab topology showing switches, host networks, ESXi, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, and controller relationships.

docs.title: Task sequence
docs.text:
1. Task 1 — Get started

  2. Task 2 — Create the VRF and networks

  3. Task 3 — Attach and deploy the networks

  4. Task 4 — Verify baseline connectivity

  5. Task 5 — Enable Secure VRF

  6. Task 6 — Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI

  7. Task 7 — Verify policy behavior

  8. Task 8 — Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Great Job! You have accomplished all the Lab Tasks. Please close any open browser tabs to keep the workspace clean.

In this lab, you explored Smart Switches and Hypershield integration and tested policy enforcement with On-prem as well as Cloud solution (SCC). You are now ready to dive deeper into these technologies and their ecosystem.

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.

vm:~$ ping 40.0.0.20
PING 40.0.0.20 (40.0.0.20): 56 data bytes

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.title: Topology
docs.text: Figure 1. Portrait lab topology showing switches, host networks, ESXi, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, and controller relationships.

docs.title: Task sequence
docs.text:
1. Task 1 — Get started

  2. Task 2 — Create the VRF and networks

  3. Task 3 — Attach and deploy the networks

  4. Task 4 — Verify baseline connectivity

  5. Task 5 — Enable Secure VRF

  6. Task 6 — Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI

  7. Task 7 — Verify policy behavior

  8. Task 8 — Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Great Job! You have accomplished all the Lab Tasks. Please close any open browser tabs to keep the workspace clean.

In this lab, you explored Smart Switches and Hypershield integration and tested policy enforcement with On-prem as well as Cloud solution (SCC). You are now ready to dive deeper into these technologies and their ecosystem.

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.title: Topology
docs.text: Figure 1. Portrait lab topology showing switches, host networks, ESXi, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, and controller relationships.

docs.title: Task sequence
docs.text:
1. Task 1 — Get started

  2. Task 2 — Create the VRF and networks

  3. Task 3 — Attach and deploy the networks

  4. Task 4 — Verify baseline connectivity

  5. Task 5 — Enable Secure VRF

  6. Task 6 — Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI

  7. Task 7 — Verify policy behavior

  8. Task 8 — Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Great Job! You have accomplished all the Lab Tasks. Please close any open browser tabs to keep the workspace clean.

In this lab, you explored Smart Switches and Hypershield integration and tested policy enforcement with On-prem as well as Cloud solution (SCC). You are now ready to dive deeper into these technologies and their ecosystem.

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.text: Figure 1. Portrait lab topology showing switches, host networks, ESXi, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, and controller relationships.

docs.title: Task sequence
docs.text:
1. Task 1 — Get started

  2. Task 2 — Create the VRF and networks

  3. Task 3 — Attach and deploy the networks

  4. Task 4 — Verify baseline connectivity

  5. Task 5 — Enable Secure VRF

  6. Task 6 — Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI

  7. Task 7 — Verify policy behavior

  8. Task 8 — Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control

docs.text:
Great Job! You have accomplished all the Lab Tasks. Please close any open browser tabs to keep the workspace clean.

In this lab, you explored Smart Switches and Hypershield integration and tested policy enforcement with On-prem as well as Cloud solution (SCC). You are now ready to dive deeper into these technologies and their ecosystem.

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.title: Topology
docs.text: Figure 1. Portrait lab topology showing switches, host networks, ESXi, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, and controller relationships.

docs.title: Task sequence
docs.text:
1. Task 1 — Get started

  2. Task 2 — Create the VRF and networks

  3. Task 3 — Attach and deploy the networks

  4. Task 4 — Verify baseline connectivity

  5. Task 5 — Enable Secure VRF

  6. Task 6 — Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI

  7. Task 7 — Verify policy behavior

  8. Task 8 — Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Great Job! You have accomplished all the Lab Tasks. Please close any open browser tabs to keep the workspace clean.

In this lab, you explored Smart Switches and Hypershield integration and tested policy enforcement with On-prem as well as Cloud solution (SCC). You are now ready to dive deeper into these technologies and their ecosystem.

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.text:
1. Task 1 — Get started

  2. Task 2 — Create the VRF and networks

  3. Task 3 — Attach and deploy the networks

  4. Task 4 — Verify baseline connectivity

  5. Task 5 — Enable Secure VRF

  6. Task 6 — Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI

  7. Task 7 — Verify policy behavior

  8. Task 8 — Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control

docs.text:
Great Job! You have accomplished all the Lab Tasks. Please close any open browser tabs to keep the workspace clean.

In this lab, you explored Smart Switches and Hypershield integration and tested policy enforcement with On-prem as well as Cloud solution (SCC). You are now ready to dive deeper into these technologies and their ecosystem.

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.

docs.title: ICMP check: from EP-vlan13, run the ping command below and record the actual response. Ping will drop

vm:~$ ping 14.0.0.20
PING 14.0.0.20 (14.0.0.20): 56 data bytes

On EP-vlan13, start the client:

vm:~$ iperf3 -c 14.0.0.20 -p 8080 -t 10 -b 1G

docs.title: Task 6: Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI
Task 6: Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI
Objective
docs.text: Because Secure VRF redirects traffic to a DPU, application traffic needs an explicit security policy. Create network objects for the two endpoint subnets in the lab VRF, then deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy from vlan13 to vlan14 and block rest of the traffic.

docs.title: Check the switch before policy creation
docs.text:
Before creating the policy, check the current switch state.

Open the saved Smart Switch session in MTPuTTY and run the command below to check for loaded policies:

Smart-SW-1# run bash sudo docker exec -it HypershieldAgent ./agwctl policies show
Client got: ok
Data:
No policies loaded
Smart-SW-1#

The switch reports no policies by default. Create and deploy the policy from the on-premises Hypershield (Timescape UI) controller.

Note: Since this is a shared lab, you might come across some policies already created by other lab users.

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.title: Topology
docs.text: Figure 1. Portrait lab topology showing switches, host networks, ESXi, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, and controller relationships.

docs.title: Task sequence
docs.text:
1. Task 1 — Get started

  2. Task 2 — Create the VRF and networks

  3. Task 3 — Attach and deploy the networks

  4. Task 4 — Verify baseline connectivity

  5. Task 5 — Enable Secure VRF

  6. Task 6 — Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI

  7. Task 7 — Verify policy behavior

  8. Task 8 — Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Great Job! You have accomplished all the Lab Tasks. Please close any open browser tabs to keep the workspace clean.

In this lab, you explored Smart Switches and Hypershield integration and tested policy enforcement with On-prem as well as Cloud solution (SCC). You are now ready to dive deeper into these technologies and their ecosystem.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Open the assigned pod systems and confirm that the required management sessions are available.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Your event lab credentials and assigned pod number.

  • Cisco Secure Client VPN access if required by the event environment.

  • Remote Desktop Connection.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Connect to the event VPN with the IP address as per your Lab access instructions.

  2. Open Remote Desktop Connection and connect to the workstation address on the pod-specific values at the start of this guide.

  3. Sign in with the credentials provided for the lab.

  4. Open the saved browser bookmarks for Nexus Dashboard and Timescape. Dashboard is the fabric configuration interface; Timescape is used later for security objects and policies.

  5. Open MTPuTTY and locate the saved sessions for both Smart Switches and both endpoints.

  6. Review the pod-specific values in this guide. Use endpoint management addresses to connect to endpoint consoles and data addresses only for traffic tests.

Checkpoint: Confirm that you can reach the workstation, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, both Smart Switches, and both endpoints. Do not change device settings yet.

The recording begins with the applications already available and does not show VPN sign-in or account onboarding. Use the event lab instructions for credentials and initial access.

docs.title: Task 2: Create the VRF and networks
Task 2: Create the VRF and networks
Create the tenant VRF and two Layer 3 networks using the assigned pod values.
docs.text: For routed communication between VXLAN EVPN networks, create a tenant VRF associated with a Layer 3 VNI. Create each Layer 3 network with its VLAN and anycast gateway, then associate it with that VRF.

docs.title: Pod values: labusr20
docs.text: The tables below contain this guide's pod-specific values.

docs.title: Create the VRF

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.

Objective

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.title: Topology
docs.text: Figure 1. Portrait lab topology showing switches, host networks, ESXi, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, and controller relationships.

docs.title: Task sequence
docs.text:
1. Task 1 — Get started

  2. Task 2 — Create the VRF and networks

  3. Task 3 — Attach and deploy the networks

  4. Task 4 — Verify baseline connectivity

  5. Task 5 — Enable Secure VRF

  6. Task 6 — Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI

  7. Task 7 — Verify policy behavior

  8. Task 8 — Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Great Job! You have accomplished all the Lab Tasks. Please close any open browser tabs to keep the workspace clean.

In this lab, you explored Smart Switches and Hypershield integration and tested policy enforcement with On-prem as well as Cloud solution (SCC). You are now ready to dive deeper into these technologies and their ecosystem.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Open the assigned pod systems and confirm that the required management sessions are available.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Your event lab credentials and assigned pod number.

  • Cisco Secure Client VPN access if required by the event environment.

  • Remote Desktop Connection.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Connect to the event VPN with the IP address as per your Lab access instructions.

  2. Open Remote Desktop Connection and connect to the workstation address on the pod-specific values at the start of this guide.

  3. Sign in with the credentials provided for the lab.

  4. Open the saved browser bookmarks for Nexus Dashboard and Timescape. Dashboard is the fabric configuration interface; Timescape is used later for security objects and policies.

  5. Open MTPuTTY and locate the saved sessions for both Smart Switches and both endpoints.

  6. Review the pod-specific values in this guide. Use endpoint management addresses to connect to endpoint consoles and data addresses only for traffic tests.

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text:
Checkpoint: Confirm that you can reach the workstation, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, both Smart Switches, and both endpoints. Do not change device settings yet.

The recording begins with the applications already available and does not show VPN sign-in or account onboarding. Use the event lab instructions for credentials and initial access.

docs.title: Task 2: Create the VRF and networks
Task 2: Create the VRF and networks
Create the tenant VRF and two Layer 3 networks using the assigned pod values.
docs.text: For routed communication between VXLAN EVPN networks, create a tenant VRF associated with a Layer 3 VNI. Create each Layer 3 network with its VLAN and anycast gateway, then associate it with that VRF.

docs.title: Pod values: labusr21
docs.text: The tables below contain this guide's pod-specific values.

docs.title: Create the VRF
docs.text:
1. Log in Nexus Dashboard with the Pod specific credential (labusr21/Dmzpassword21), open Manage > Fabrics > SmartSwitch-Pod1 > Segmentation and security > VRFs. Select Actions (white) > Create.

  2. In the Create VRF wizard, enter the values in the VRF table.

Parameter Value or Selection VRF name labusr21-vrf Tenant labusr21-tn VRF ID Keep the default value (50000) VLAN ID Click on “Propose VLAN” VRF VLAN name labusr21-vrf VRF interface description labusr21-vrf

Figure. Create VRF wizard with pod values entered.

  1. Click Create to save the VRF.

Figure. Created tenant-scoped VRF and its assigned ID.

docs.title: Create the networks
docs.text:
Layer 2 VNIs map VLAN-backed network segments. For this routed lab, create two Layer 3 networks, assign their VLAN IDs and anycast gateways, and associate both with the tenant VRF.

  1. In the top navigation click the Networks tab, then select Actions (white) > Create.

  2. Enter the following values for vlan51.

Parameter Value or Selection Network Name vlan51 Tenant labusr21-tn Network mode Layer3 VRF name labusr21-vrf (select from drop-down) Network ID Keep the default value VLAN ID 51 IPv4 gateway/netmask 51.0.0.1/24 VLAN name vlan51

Figure. vlan51 network configuration.

  1. Click Create to save vlan51.
  1. Create the second network vlan52 and enter the values from this table.
Parameter Value or Selection Network Name vlan52 Tenant labusr21-tn Network mode Layer3 VRF name labusr21-vrf (select from drop-down) Network ID Keep the default value VLAN ID 52 IPv4 gateway/netmask 52.0.0.1/24 VLAN name vlan52
  1. Click Create to save vlan52.

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text:
Checkpoint: Confirm that vlan51 and vlan52 appear with their assigned network IDs, VLAN IDs, and gateway prefixes. The screenshot shows example IDs 30000 and 30001; use the IDs assigned by your pod. Network attachment and deployment are completed in Task 3.

Figure. vlan51 and vlan52 rows with recorded IDs and gateways.

docs.title: Task 3: Attach and Deploy the networks
Task 3: Attach and Deploy the networks
Objective
docs.text: Attach vlan51 to Smart-SW-1 Ethernet1/13 and vlan52 to Smart-SW-2 Ethernet1/13, following the supplied host-to-switch design. This guide deploys the VRF first, then the two networks.

docs.title: Attach the networks
docs.text:
1. Attach vlan51 to Smart-SW-1 Ethernet1/13.

    • a. In SmartSwitch-Pod1, open Segmentation and security > Networks.

    • b. Click vlan51, then click Network Attachments.

    • c. Select the check box which has an entry of Smart-SW-1 switch, then click white Actions > Edit

    • d. In the Edit Network Attachment screen, click the slider to Attach, then under Attached interface for this device click (white) Action and click on Add network interface attachment

      Figure. Network attachment editor for vlan51.

    • e. Under Add Network Interface Attachment, filter with Smart-SW-1 and Ethernet 1/13

      Figure. Select Smart-SW-1 Ethernet1/13 for vlan51.

      Figure. Selected interface for the vlan51 attachment.

    • f. Click Add, then Save the attachment.

      Figure. vlan51 interface attachment in the edit view.

    • g. Return to the Networks view

      Figure. vlan51 attached to Smart-SW-1.

  2. Attach vlan52 to Smart-SW-2 Ethernet1/13.

    • a. Click vlan52, then open Network Attachments tab.

    • b. Select the check box which has an entry of Smart-SW-2 switch then click white Actions > Edit.

    • c. In the Edit Network Attachment screen, click the slider to Attach then under Attached interface for this device click (white) Action and click on Add network interface attachment.

    • d. Under Add Network Interface Attachment, filter with Smart-SW-2 and Ethernet 1/13

    • e. Click Add and then click Save

      Figure. vlan52 attachment for Smart-SW-2.

    • f. Return to the Networks view

      Figure. Network table after attachments are staged.

Both network attachments are staged in Nexus Dashboard. Deploy the VRF first, then deploy the networks.

docs.title: Deploy the VRF
docs.text:
1. Open Segmentation and security > VRFs.

  2. Select labusr21-vrf, then choose Actions (white) > Deploy.

Figure. VRF deployment action.

Figure. Pending VRF configuration review.

Figure. VRF deployment status.

Figure. labusr21-vrf is deployed.

docs.title: Deploy the networks
docs.text:
After the VRF is deployed, deploy both network configurations.

  1. Open Segmentation and security > Networks.

  2. Select vlan51 and vlan52, then choose Actions (white) > Deploy.

Figure. Pending network configuration review.

  1. Review the pending configuration, click Deploy, and select when it gets completed, click Close.

docs.title: Checkpoint

Checkpoint: Confirm that both networks show Deployed and that each attachment is Attached to the expected switch and its interface. The recording showed successful configuration synchronization.

Figure. Both networks show Deployed.

docs.text: Enable Secure VRF on both switches and verify Hypershield agent and forwarding readiness.

docs.title: Enable Secure VRF
docs.text:
1. Log in Nexus Dashboard with the Pod specific credential (labusr21/Dmzpassword21), open Manage > Fabrics > SmartSwitch-Pod1 > Segmentation and security > VRFs.

  2. Select labusr21-vrf, then choose Actions (white) > Multi-attach and select both Smart Switches and click Next.

Figure. Secure VRF save and deploy wizard.

Figure. Pending Secure VRF configuration.

  1. Log in to Smart-SW-1 and Smart-SW-2 via MTPuTTY and run both commands:

    #show running-config service-acceleration
#show service-acceleration status detail

    Come back to the Nexus Dashboard, review the pending configuration, and select Deploy all. When deployment completes, select Close.

docs.title: Verify switch readiness
docs.text:
Confirm that the output reports Agent Health Status: ok, a successful controller connection, firewall in-service, and VRF operational state forwarding ready. The recording showed Dynamic affinity and DPU 2 for labusr21-t:labusr21-vrf.

Figure. Hypershield agent and service acceleration report ready.

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.

docs.title: ICMP check: from EP-vlan51, run the ping command below and record the actual response. Ping will drop
docs.text:
vm:~$ ping 52.0.0.20
PING 52.0.0.20 (52.0.0.20): 56 data bytes

docs.title: TCP/8080 check: start the server on EP-vlan52, then the client on EP-vlan51. Before the allow policy exists, record whether the connection is blocked.
docs.text:
On EP-vlan52, start the server:

vm:~$ iperf3 -s -p 8080

On EP-vlan51, start the client:

vm:~$ iperf3 -c 52.0.0.20 -p 8080 -t 10 -b 1G

docs.title: Task 6: Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI
Task 6: Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI
Objective
docs.text: Because Secure VRF redirects traffic to a DPU, application traffic needs an explicit security policy. Create network objects for the two endpoint subnets in the lab VRF, then deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy from vlan51 to vlan52 and block rest of the traffic.

docs.title: Check the switch before policy creation
docs.text:
Before creating the policy, check the current switch state.

Open the saved Smart Switch session in MTPuTTY and run the command below to check for loaded policies:

Smart-SW-1# run bash sudo docker exec -it HypershieldAgent ./agwctl policies show
Client got: ok
Data:
No policies loaded
Smart-SW-1#

The switch reports no policies by default. Create and deploy the policy from the on-premises Hypershield (Timescape UI) controller.

Note: Since this is a shared lab, you might come across some policies already created by other lab users.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: The deployed policy permits TCP port 8080 between the configured networks. Other protocols, including ICMP, are not permitted by this rule and are expected to be denied.

Task 8: Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control
Objective

  3. Find the pod-specific policy (vlan51-52 for POD-21), and click on three dots > Edit > Deploy.

Figure. Open the policy for editing in Security Cloud Control.

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.title: Topology
docs.text: Figure 1. Portrait lab topology showing switches, host networks, ESXi, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, and controller relationships.

docs.title: Task sequence
docs.text:
1. Task 1 — Get started

  2. Task 2 — Create the VRF and networks

  3. Task 3 — Attach and deploy the networks

  4. Task 4 — Verify baseline connectivity

  5. Task 5 — Enable Secure VRF

  6. Task 6 — Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI

  7. Task 7 — Verify policy behavior

  8. Task 8 — Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Great Job! You have accomplished all the Lab Tasks. Please close any open browser tabs to keep the workspace clean.

In this lab, you explored Smart Switches and Hypershield integration and tested policy enforcement with On-prem as well as Cloud solution (SCC). You are now ready to dive deeper into these technologies and their ecosystem.

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.title: Topology
docs.text: Figure 1. Portrait lab topology showing switches, host networks, ESXi, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, and controller relationships.

docs.title: Task sequence
docs.text:
1. Task 1 — Get started

  2. Task 2 — Create the VRF and networks

  3. Task 3 — Attach and deploy the networks

  4. Task 4 — Verify baseline connectivity

  5. Task 5 — Enable Secure VRF

  6. Task 6 — Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI

  7. Task 7 — Verify policy behavior

  8. Task 8 — Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Great Job! You have accomplished all the Lab Tasks. Please close any open browser tabs to keep the workspace clean.

In this lab, you explored Smart Switches and Hypershield integration and tested policy enforcement with On-prem as well as Cloud solution (SCC). You are now ready to dive deeper into these technologies and their ecosystem.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Open the assigned pod systems and confirm that the required management sessions are available.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:

  • Remote Desktop Connection.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Connect to the event VPN with the IP address as per your Lab access instructions.

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.

vm:~$ ping 56.0.0.20
PING 56.0.0.20 (56.0.0.20): 56 data bytes

On EP-vlan55, start the client:

vm:~$ iperf3 -c 56.0.0.20 -p 8080 -t 10 -b 1G

Task 6: Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI
Objective

Before creating the policy, check the current switch state.

Open the saved Smart Switch session in MTPuTTY and run the command below to check for loaded policies:

Smart-SW-1# run bash sudo docker exec -it HypershieldAgent ./agwctl policies show
Client got: ok
Data:
No policies loaded
Smart-SW-1#

The switch reports no policies by default. Create and deploy the policy from the on-premises Hypershield (Timescape UI) controller.

Note: Since this is a shared lab, you might come across some policies already created by other lab users.

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.text: Figure 1. Portrait lab topology showing switches, host networks, ESXi, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, and controller relationships.

docs.title: Task sequence
docs.text:
1. Task 1 — Get started

  2. Task 2 — Create the VRF and networks

  3. Task 3 — Attach and deploy the networks

  4. Task 4 — Verify baseline connectivity

  5. Task 5 — Enable Secure VRF

  6. Task 6 — Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI

  7. Task 7 — Verify policy behavior

  8. Task 8 — Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Great Job! You have accomplished all the Lab Tasks. Please close any open browser tabs to keep the workspace clean.

In this lab, you explored Smart Switches and Hypershield integration and tested policy enforcement with On-prem as well as Cloud solution (SCC). You are now ready to dive deeper into these technologies and their ecosystem.

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.

PING 58.0.0.20 (58.0.0.20): 56 data bytes

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.title: Topology
docs.text: Figure 1. Portrait lab topology showing switches, host networks, ESXi, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, and controller relationships.

docs.title: Task sequence
docs.text:
1. Task 1 — Get started

  2. Task 2 — Create the VRF and networks

  3. Task 3 — Attach and deploy the networks

  4. Task 4 — Verify baseline connectivity

  5. Task 5 — Enable Secure VRF

  6. Task 6 — Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI

  7. Task 7 — Verify policy behavior

  8. Task 8 — Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Great Job! You have accomplished all the Lab Tasks. Please close any open browser tabs to keep the workspace clean.

In this lab, you explored Smart Switches and Hypershield integration and tested policy enforcement with On-prem as well as Cloud solution (SCC). You are now ready to dive deeper into these technologies and their ecosystem.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Open the assigned pod systems and confirm that the required management sessions are available.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Your event lab credentials and assigned pod number.

  • Cisco Secure Client VPN access if required by the event environment.

  • Remote Desktop Connection.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Connect to the event VPN with the IP address as per your Lab access instructions.

  2. Open Remote Desktop Connection and connect to the workstation address on the pod-specific values at the start of this guide.

  3. Sign in with the credentials provided for the lab.

  4. Open the saved browser bookmarks for Nexus Dashboard and Timescape. Dashboard is the fabric configuration interface; Timescape is used later for security objects and policies.

  5. Open MTPuTTY and locate the saved sessions for both Smart Switches and both endpoints.

  6. Review the pod-specific values in this guide. Use endpoint management addresses to connect to endpoint consoles and data addresses only for traffic tests.

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.

vm:~$ ping 60.0.0.20
PING 60.0.0.20 (60.0.0.20): 56 data bytes

On EP-vlan59, start the client:

vm:~$ iperf3 -c 60.0.0.20 -p 8080 -t 10 -b 1G

docs.title: Task 8: Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control
Task 8: Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control
Objective
docs.text: Create and manage the Hypershield network objects and policy through Security Cloud Control (SCC), then verify policy deployment and endpoint connectivity.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Launch Security Cloud Control in the browser and sign in with the credentials provided for the lab.

  2. Open Organization > Product > Hypershield > Policy.

  3. Find the pod-specific policy (vlan59-60 for POD-25), and click on three dots > Edit > Deploy.

Figure. Open the policy for editing in Security Cloud Control.

  1. On the Edit Policy page, select ICMP. Keep TCP port 8080 enabled, then click Deploy.

Figure. Permit ICMP along with TCP port 8080.

docs.text:
1. To experience the object and policy deployment process via SCC, remove your existing objects and policies from the on-premises Timescape environment. Once they are cleared, proceed with Task 6: Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI.

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.title: Topology
docs.text: Figure 1. Portrait lab topology showing switches, host networks, ESXi, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, and controller relationships.

docs.title: Task sequence
docs.text:
1. Task 1 — Get started

  2. Task 2 — Create the VRF and networks

  3. Task 3 — Attach and deploy the networks

  4. Task 4 — Verify baseline connectivity

  5. Task 5 — Enable Secure VRF

  6. Task 6 — Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI

  7. Task 7 — Verify policy behavior

  8. Task 8 — Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Great Job! You have accomplished all the Lab Tasks. Please close any open browser tabs to keep the workspace clean.

In this lab, you explored Smart Switches and Hypershield integration and tested policy enforcement with On-prem as well as Cloud solution (SCC). You are now ready to dive deeper into these technologies and their ecosystem.

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.

PING 62.0.0.20 (62.0.0.20): 56 data bytes

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: The deployed policy permits TCP port 8080 between the configured networks. Other protocols, including ICMP, are not permitted by this rule and are expected to be denied.

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.title: Topology
docs.text: Figure 1. Portrait lab topology showing switches, host networks, ESXi, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, and controller relationships.

docs.title: Task sequence
docs.text:
1. Task 1 — Get started

  2. Task 2 — Create the VRF and networks

  3. Task 3 — Attach and deploy the networks

  4. Task 4 — Verify baseline connectivity

  5. Task 5 — Enable Secure VRF

  6. Task 6 — Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI

  7. Task 7 — Verify policy behavior

  8. Task 8 — Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Great Job! You have accomplished all the Lab Tasks. Please close any open browser tabs to keep the workspace clean.

In this lab, you explored Smart Switches and Hypershield integration and tested policy enforcement with On-prem as well as Cloud solution (SCC). You are now ready to dive deeper into these technologies and their ecosystem.

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.

Objective

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.title: Topology
docs.text: Figure 1. Portrait lab topology showing switches, host networks, ESXi, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, and controller relationships.

docs.title: Task sequence
docs.text:
1. Task 1 — Get started

  2. Task 2 — Create the VRF and networks

  3. Task 3 — Attach and deploy the networks

  4. Task 4 — Verify baseline connectivity

  5. Task 5 — Enable Secure VRF

  6. Task 6 — Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI

  7. Task 7 — Verify policy behavior

  8. Task 8 — Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Great Job! You have accomplished all the Lab Tasks. Please close any open browser tabs to keep the workspace clean.

In this lab, you explored Smart Switches and Hypershield integration and tested policy enforcement with On-prem as well as Cloud solution (SCC). You are now ready to dive deeper into these technologies and their ecosystem.

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.

PING 66.0.0.20 (66.0.0.20): 56 data bytes

docs.title: Task 6: Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI
Task 6: Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI
Objective
docs.text: Because Secure VRF redirects traffic to a DPU, application traffic needs an explicit security policy. Create network objects for the two endpoint subnets in the lab VRF, then deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy from vlan65 to vlan66 and block rest of the traffic.

docs.title: Check the switch before policy creation
docs.text:
Before creating the policy, check the current switch state.

Open the saved Smart Switch session in MTPuTTY and run the command below to check for loaded policies:

Smart-SW-1# run bash sudo docker exec -it HypershieldAgent ./agwctl policies show
Client got: ok
Data:
No policies loaded
Smart-SW-1#

The switch reports no policies by default. Create and deploy the policy from the on-premises Hypershield (Timescape UI) controller.

Note: Since this is a shared lab, you might come across some policies already created by other lab users.

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.
