docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.title: Topology
docs.text: Figure 1. Portrait lab topology showing switches, host networks, ESXi, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, and controller relationships.

docs.title: Task sequence
docs.text:
1. Task 1 — Get started

  2. Task 2 — Create the VRF and networks

  3. Task 3 — Attach and deploy the networks

  4. Task 4 — Verify baseline connectivity

  5. Task 5 — Enable Secure VRF

  6. Task 6 — Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI

  7. Task 7 — Verify policy behavior

  8. Task 8 — Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Great Job! You have accomplished all the Lab Tasks. Please close any open browser tabs to keep the workspace clean.

In this lab, you explored Smart Switches and Hypershield integration and tested policy enforcement with On-prem as well as Cloud solution (SCC). You are now ready to dive deeper into these technologies and their ecosystem.

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.

vm:~$ ping 16.0.0.20
PING 16.0.0.20 (16.0.0.20): 56 data bytes

On EP-vlan15, start the client:

vm:~$ iperf3 -c 16.0.0.20 -p 8080 -t 10 -b 1G

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.title: Topology
docs.text: Figure 1. Portrait lab topology showing switches, host networks, ESXi, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, and controller relationships.

docs.title: Task sequence
docs.text:
1. Task 1 — Get started

  2. Task 2 — Create the VRF and networks

  3. Task 3 — Attach and deploy the networks

  4. Task 4 — Verify baseline connectivity

  5. Task 5 — Enable Secure VRF

  6. Task 6 — Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI

  7. Task 7 — Verify policy behavior

  8. Task 8 — Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Great Job! You have accomplished all the Lab Tasks. Please close any open browser tabs to keep the workspace clean.

In this lab, you explored Smart Switches and Hypershield integration and tested policy enforcement with On-prem as well as Cloud solution (SCC). You are now ready to dive deeper into these technologies and their ecosystem.

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.

vm:~$ ping 70.0.0.20
PING 70.0.0.20 (70.0.0.20): 56 data bytes

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.text: Figure 1. Portrait lab topology showing switches, host networks, ESXi, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, and controller relationships.

docs.title: Task sequence
docs.text:
1. Task 1 — Get started

  2. Task 2 — Create the VRF and networks

  3. Task 3 — Attach and deploy the networks

  4. Task 4 — Verify baseline connectivity

  5. Task 5 — Enable Secure VRF

  6. Task 6 — Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI

  7. Task 7 — Verify policy behavior

  8. Task 8 — Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Great Job! You have accomplished all the Lab Tasks. Please close any open browser tabs to keep the workspace clean.

In this lab, you explored Smart Switches and Hypershield integration and tested policy enforcement with On-prem as well as Cloud solution (SCC). You are now ready to dive deeper into these technologies and their ecosystem.

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.title: Topology
docs.text: Figure 1. Portrait lab topology showing switches, host networks, ESXi, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, and controller relationships.

docs.title: Task sequence
docs.text:
1. Task 1 — Get started

  2. Task 2 — Create the VRF and networks

  3. Task 3 — Attach and deploy the networks

  4. Task 4 — Verify baseline connectivity

  5. Task 5 — Enable Secure VRF

  6. Task 6 — Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI

  7. Task 7 — Verify policy behavior

  8. Task 8 — Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Great Job! You have accomplished all the Lab Tasks. Please close any open browser tabs to keep the workspace clean.

In this lab, you explored Smart Switches and Hypershield integration and tested policy enforcement with On-prem as well as Cloud solution (SCC). You are now ready to dive deeper into these technologies and their ecosystem.

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.text: Figure 1. Portrait lab topology showing switches, host networks, ESXi, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, and controller relationships.

docs.title: Task sequence
docs.text:
1. Task 1 — Get started

  2. Task 2 — Create the VRF and networks

  3. Task 3 — Attach and deploy the networks

  4. Task 4 — Verify baseline connectivity

  5. Task 5 — Enable Secure VRF

  6. Task 6 — Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI

  7. Task 7 — Verify policy behavior

  8. Task 8 — Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control

docs.text:
Great Job! You have accomplished all the Lab Tasks. Please close any open browser tabs to keep the workspace clean.

In this lab, you explored Smart Switches and Hypershield integration and tested policy enforcement with On-prem as well as Cloud solution (SCC). You are now ready to dive deeper into these technologies and their ecosystem.

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.title: Topology
docs.text: Figure 1. Portrait lab topology showing switches, host networks, ESXi, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, and controller relationships.

docs.title: Task sequence
docs.text:
1. Task 1 — Get started

  2. Task 2 — Create the VRF and networks

  3. Task 3 — Attach and deploy the networks

  4. Task 4 — Verify baseline connectivity

  5. Task 5 — Enable Secure VRF

  6. Task 6 — Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI

  7. Task 7 — Verify policy behavior

  8. Task 8 — Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Great Job! You have accomplished all the Lab Tasks. Please close any open browser tabs to keep the workspace clean.

In this lab, you explored Smart Switches and Hypershield integration and tested policy enforcement with On-prem as well as Cloud solution (SCC). You are now ready to dive deeper into these technologies and their ecosystem.

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.text:
1. Task 1 — Get started

  2. Task 2 — Create the VRF and networks

  3. Task 3 — Attach and deploy the networks

  4. Task 4 — Verify baseline connectivity

  5. Task 5 — Enable Secure VRF

  6. Task 6 — Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI

  7. Task 7 — Verify policy behavior

  8. Task 8 — Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control

docs.text:
Great Job! You have accomplished all the Lab Tasks. Please close any open browser tabs to keep the workspace clean.

In this lab, you explored Smart Switches and Hypershield integration and tested policy enforcement with On-prem as well as Cloud solution (SCC). You are now ready to dive deeper into these technologies and their ecosystem.

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.

docs.title: ICMP check: from EP-vlan25, run the ping command below and record the actual response. Ping will drop

vm:~$ ping 26.0.0.20
PING 26.0.0.20 (26.0.0.20): 56 data bytes

On EP-vlan25, start the client:

vm:~$ iperf3 -c 26.0.0.20 -p 8080 -t 10 -b 1G

docs.title: Task 6: Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI
Task 6: Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI
Objective
docs.text: Because Secure VRF redirects traffic to a DPU, application traffic needs an explicit security policy. Create network objects for the two endpoint subnets in the lab VRF, then deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy from vlan25 to vlan26 and block rest of the traffic.

docs.title: Check the switch before policy creation
docs.text:
Before creating the policy, check the current switch state.

Open the saved Smart Switch session in MTPuTTY and run the command below to check for loaded policies:

Smart-SW-1# run bash sudo docker exec -it HypershieldAgent ./agwctl policies show
Client got: ok
Data:
No policies loaded
Smart-SW-1#

The switch reports no policies by default. Create and deploy the policy from the on-premises Hypershield (Timescape UI) controller.

Note: Since this is a shared lab, you might come across some policies already created by other lab users.

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
• Create a tenant-scoped VRF and two Layer 3 networks in Nexus Dashboard.

  • Attach and deploy the networks on the assigned Smart Switch interfaces.

  • Verify baseline connectivity and switch-side Hypershield readiness.

  • Create scoped Timescape objects and a TCP/8080 allow policy.

  • Rerun connectivity analysis and record live endpoint test results.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: In this lab, use Nexus Dashboard to configure two tenant-scoped Layer 3 networks on a Cisco Smart Switch pair, verify baseline connectivity, enable Secure VRF redirection, and deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy through Timescape.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Start with routed networks and verify baseline connectivity. Then enable Secure VRF and inspect switch-side Hypershield readiness. Before a matching policy exists, review the pre-policy analysis. Create the network objects and TCP/8080 allow policy in Timescape, then rerun analysis and test permitted and denied traffic.

docs.title: Topology
docs.text: Figure 1. Portrait lab topology showing switches, host networks, ESXi, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, and controller relationships.

docs.title: Task sequence
docs.text:
1. Task 1 — Get started

  2. Task 2 — Create the VRF and networks

  3. Task 3 — Attach and deploy the networks

  4. Task 4 — Verify baseline connectivity

  5. Task 5 — Enable Secure VRF

  6. Task 6 — Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI

  7. Task 7 — Verify policy behavior

  8. Task 8 — Create/Manage objects and policy via Security Cloud Control

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Great Job! You have accomplished all the Lab Tasks. Please close any open browser tabs to keep the workspace clean.

In this lab, you explored Smart Switches and Hypershield integration and tested policy enforcement with On-prem as well as Cloud solution (SCC). You are now ready to dive deeper into these technologies and their ecosystem.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Open the assigned pod systems and confirm that the required management sessions are available.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Your event lab credentials and assigned pod number.

  • Cisco Secure Client VPN access if required by the event environment.

  • Remote Desktop Connection.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Connect to the event VPN with the IP address as per your Lab access instructions.

  2. Open Remote Desktop Connection and connect to the workstation address on the pod-specific values at the start of this guide.

  3. Sign in with the credentials provided for the lab.

  4. Open the saved browser bookmarks for Nexus Dashboard and Timescape. Dashboard is the fabric configuration interface; Timescape is used later for security objects and policies.

  5. Open MTPuTTY and locate the saved sessions for both Smart Switches and both endpoints.

  6. Review the pod-specific values in this guide. Use endpoint management addresses to connect to endpoint consoles and data addresses only for traffic tests.

Checkpoint: Confirm that you can reach the workstation, Nexus Dashboard, Timescape, both Smart Switches, and both endpoints. Do not change device settings yet.

The recording begins with the applications already available and does not show VPN sign-in or account onboarding. Use the event lab instructions for credentials and initial access.

docs.title: Task 2: Create the VRF and networks
Task 2: Create the VRF and networks
Create the tenant VRF and two Layer 3 networks using the assigned pod values.
docs.text: For routed communication between VXLAN EVPN networks, create a tenant VRF associated with a Layer 3 VNI. Create each Layer 3 network with its VLAN and anycast gateway, then associate it with that VRF.

docs.title: Pod values: labusr09
docs.text: The tables below contain this guide's pod-specific values.

docs.title: Create the VRF
docs.text:

docs.title: Task 3: Attach and Deploy the networks

Objective
docs.text: Attach vlan27 to Smart-SW-1 Ethernet1/13 and vlan28 to Smart-SW-2 Ethernet1/13, following the supplied host-to-switch design. This guide deploys the VRF first, then the two networks.

docs.title: Attach the networks
docs.text:
1. Attach vlan27 to Smart-SW-1 Ethernet1/13.

    • a. In SmartSwitch-Pod1, open Segmentation and security > Networks.

    • g. Return to the Networks view

docs.text:
Confirm that the output reports Agent Health Status: ok, a successful controller connection, firewall in-service, and VRF operational state forwarding ready. The recording showed Dynamic affinity and DPU 2 for labusr09-t:labusr09-vrf.

Figure. Hypershield agent and service acceleration report ready.

docs.title: Expected traffic before policy deployment
docs.text: When VRF traffic is redirected to the DPU and no explicit security policies exist from Hypershield, then the default behavior is to block traffic. This means the application will break because no permit policy allows the traffic through the DPU. This default deny enforcement ensures that without explicit permission, no communication is allowed, which is a Security best practice.

docs.title: ICMP check: from EP-vlan27, run the ping command below and record the actual response. Ping will drop
docs.text:
vm:~$ ping 28.0.0.20
PING 28.0.0.20 (28.0.0.20): 56 data bytes

docs.text:
On EP-vlan28, start the server:

vm:~$ iperf3 -s -p 8080

On EP-vlan27, start the client:

vm:~$ iperf3 -c 28.0.0.20 -p 8080 -t 10 -b 1G

docs.title: Task 6: Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI
Task 6: Create objects and policy via On-Premise Timescape UI
Objective
docs.text: Because Secure VRF redirects traffic to a DPU, application traffic needs an explicit security policy. Create network objects for the two endpoint subnets in the lab VRF, then deploy a TCP/8080 allow policy from vlan27 to vlan28 and block rest of the traffic.

docs.title: Check the switch before policy creation
docs.text:
Before creating the policy, check the current switch state.

Open the saved Smart Switch session in MTPuTTY and run the command below to check for loaded policies:

Smart-SW-1# run bash sudo docker exec -it HypershieldAgent ./agwctl policies show
Client got: ok
Data:
No policies loaded
Smart-SW-1#

The switch reports no policies by default. Create and deploy the policy from the on-premises Hypershield (Timescape UI) controller.

Note: Since this is a shared lab, you might come across some policies already created by other lab users.

Figure. Create Object selection in Timescape.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: The deployed policy permits TCP port 8080 between the configured networks. Other protocols, including ICMP, are not permitted by this rule and are expected to be denied.
